name: Malawi
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. IDs are TL:<subject>:<measure>:<vintage> and stable across builds: a changed value under the same ID is an upstream revision (recorded in the ledger at /ledger); a new observed year is a new claim. A null or absent figure mints no claim — absence is never zero. Scheme: https://terralore.co/integrity

claims.title: Bantu-speaking farmers settle the plateau
claims.summary: Bantu-speaking peoples moved into the Lake Malawi region during the early centuries of the Common Era, introducing ironworking and settled agriculture and absorbing or displacing earlier hunter-gatherer communities.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1-bantu-speaking-farmers-settle-the-plateau, claim TL:MWI:event:1:bantu-speaking-farmers-settle-the-plateau, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Chewa rock-painting tradition at Chongoni
claims.summary: Chewa farming communities, especially women, developed a distinctive rock-painting tradition on the granite hills of the central plateau, linked to initiation, funerals and rainmaking, building on far older paintings by BaTwa hunter-gatherers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1000-the-chewa-rock-painting-tradition-at-chongoni, claim TL:MWI:event:1000:the-chewa-rock-painting-tradition-at-chongoni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Maravi Confederacy
claims.summary: The Amaravi, ancestors of the Chewa, established a confederacy under the Kalonga on the southwestern shores of Lake Nyasa, ruling from Mankhamba — the state that gave Malawi its name.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1480-founding-of-the-maravi-confederacy, claim TL:MWI:event:1480:founding-of-the-maravi-confederacy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gaspar Bocarro crosses the region
claims.summary: The Portuguese traveller Gaspar Bocarro journeyed through the territory, leaving what is generally regarded as the first European account of the land and peoples of the future Malawi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1616-gaspar-bocarro-crosses-the-region, claim TL:MWI:event:1616:gaspar-bocarro-crosses-the-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Maravi Empire at its peak
claims.summary: In the seventeenth century the confederacy administered a broad domain reaching across parts of modern Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia, trading ivory and iron with Portuguese and Swahili merchants on the coast.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1650-the-maravi-empire-at-its-peak, claim TL:MWI:event:1650:the-maravi-empire-at-its-peak, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline of the confederacy
claims.summary: Fighting among the sub-chiefs and the spreading slave trade eroded the Kalonga's authority, and the Maravi state fragmented into smaller Chewa chiefdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1700-decline-of-the-confederacy, claim TL:MWI:event:1700:decline-of-the-confederacy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ngoni and Yao migrations reshape the region
claims.summary: Ngoni warrior bands fleeing the Mfecane settled around Lake Nyasa, while the Yao migrated from northern Mozambique and the Tumbuka occupied the northern highlands, overlaying new peoples on the older Chewa chiefdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1820-ngoni-and-yao-migrations-reshape-the-region, claim TL:MWI:event:1820:ngoni-and-yao-migrations-reshape-the-region, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Jumbe and the slave trade at Nkhotakota
claims.summary: The Swahili-Arab trader Salim bin Abdallah, the Jumbe, established himself at Nkhotakota, which became a major slaving entrepôt on the western lakeshore; the Yao became leading participants in the trade across the lake.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1840-the-jumbe-and-the-slave-trade-at-nkhotakota, claim TL:MWI:event:1840:the-jumbe-and-the-slave-trade-at-nkhotakota, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Livingstone reaches Lake Nyasa
claims.summary: David Livingstone, on the Zambezi expedition, reached Lake Nyasa and reported it as a corridor of the slave caravans, calling for commerce and Christianity to end the trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1859-livingstone-reaches-lake-nyasa, claim TL:MWI:event:1859:livingstone-reaches-lake-nyasa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Scottish missions founded at Livingstonia and Blantyre
claims.summary: Inspired by Livingstone, the Free Church of Scotland established the Livingstonia mission in 1875 and the Church of Scotland the Blantyre mission in 1876; both campaigned against the slave trade and trained an African Christian elite.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1875-scottish-missions-founded-at-livingstonia-and, claim TL:MWI:event:1875:scottish-missions-founded-at-livingstonia-and, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British Central Africa Protectorate proclaimed
claims.summary: Britain proclaimed a protectorate over the lake region and the Shire highlands, with Harry Johnston as first commissioner; he suppressed the slave trade by force and parcelled out land to European settlers through certificates of claim.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1891-british-central-africa-protectorate-proclaimed, claim TL:MWI:event:1891:british-central-africa-protectorate-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The protectorate renamed Nyasaland
claims.summary: The British Central Africa Protectorate was renamed the Nyasaland Protectorate, the name by which the territory would be known until independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1907-the-protectorate-renamed-nyasaland, claim TL:MWI:event:1907:the-protectorate-renamed-nyasaland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Chilembwe rising
claims.summary: Reverend John Chilembwe led an uprising against colonial rule, forced labour and wartime conscription; his followers attacked the A. L. Bruce estate at Magomero and killed William Jervis Livingstone before British forces swiftly suppressed the revolt.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1915-the-chilembwe-rising, claim TL:MWI:event:1915:the-chilembwe-rising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chilembwe killed
claims.summary: John Chilembwe was shot dead as he fled toward Mozambique; though the rising failed, he became an enduring symbol of Malawian nationalism and is honoured as a national martyr.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1915-chilembwe-killed, claim TL:MWI:event:1915:chilembwe-killed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Nyasaland African Congress
claims.summary: African political associations coalesced into the Nyasaland African Congress, the first territory-wide nationalist body, which would later spearhead opposition to federation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1944-founding-of-the-nyasaland-african-congress, claim TL:MWI:event:1944:founding-of-the-nyasaland-african-congress, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland created
claims.summary: Britain bound Nyasaland into a settler-dominated federation with Southern and Northern Rhodesia, provoking deep and sustained African opposition across Nyasaland.

sources.label: Formation of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1953-federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland-created, claim TL:MWI:event:1953:federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland-created, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: State of emergency and Operation Sunrise
claims.summary: Amid mounting agitation against federation, the governor declared a state of emergency and detained Banda and over a thousand Congress members; the Devlin Commission later condemned the use of force and likened Nyasaland to a police state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1959-state-of-emergency-and-operation-sunrise, claim TL:MWI:event:1959:state-of-emergency-and-operation-sunrise, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malawi Congress Party wins the elections
claims.summary: Banda's Malawi Congress Party won the 1961 legislative elections decisively, securing African control of the colonial legislature and accelerating the path to self-government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1961-malawi-congress-party-wins-the-elections, claim TL:MWI:event:1961:malawi-congress-party-wins-the-elections, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Federation dissolved
claims.summary: Faced with African opposition and irreconcilable tensions, the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland was dissolved at the end of 1963, clearing the way for the separate independence of Malawi, Zambia and Rhodesia.

sources.label: Formation of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1963-the-federation-dissolved, claim TL:MWI:event:1963:the-federation-dissolved, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malawi independent
claims.summary: Nyasaland became the independent state of Malawi within the Commonwealth, with Hastings Kamuzu Banda as prime minister; the United States recognised the new nation the same day.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Malawi
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1964-malawi-independent, claim TL:MWI:event:1964:malawi-independent, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Banda declared President for Life
claims.summary: After Malawi became a republic in 1966 with the Malawi Congress Party as sole legal party, the National Assembly in 1971 proclaimed Banda President for Life, completing the one-party state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1971-banda-declared-president-for-life, claim TL:MWI:event:1971:banda-declared-president-for-life, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Three decades of one-party rule
claims.summary: Banda ruled as life-president through the Malawi Congress Party, detaining, exiling or killing opponents and maintaining a tightly controlled, conservative and pro-Western state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1971-three-decades-of-one-party-rule, claim TL:MWI:event:1971:three-decades-of-one-party-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Referendum ends the one-party state
claims.summary: Malawians voted by roughly two to one to abandon single-party rule and adopt multiparty democracy, opening the way to free elections.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1993-referendum-ends-the-one-party-state, claim TL:MWI:event:1993:referendum-ends-the-one-party-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First multiparty elections; Banda defeated
claims.summary: In the first multiparty general election since independence, Bakili Muluzi of the United Democratic Front defeated Hastings Banda, who peacefully gave up power after three decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-1994-first-multiparty-elections-banda-defeated, claim TL:MWI:event:1994:first-multiparty-elections-banda-defeated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Joyce Banda becomes head of state
claims.summary: After the death in office of President Bingu wa Mutharika, Vice-President Joyce Banda succeeded him, becoming Malawi's first woman president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-2012-joyce-banda-becomes-head-of-state, claim TL:MWI:event:2012:joyce-banda-becomes-head-of-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Court-ordered election re-run
claims.summary: After the Constitutional Court annulled the 2019 presidential election for irregularities, Lazarus Chakwera won the court-ordered re-run, a rare judicial reversal of a presidential result on the continent.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-2020-court-ordered-election-re-run, claim TL:MWI:event:2020:court-ordered-election-re-run, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Peaceful alternation of power
claims.summary: Peter Mutharika won the 2025 general election, defeating the incumbent Lazarus Chakwera, who conceded — marking another peaceful transfer of power in multiparty Malawi.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malawi: From the Maravi Confederacy on the shores of Lake Nyasa and the Chongoni rock-painters to the slave caravans, Scottish missions, the Chilembwe rising, and independence under Kamuzu Banda.", terralore.co/country/MWI/chronicle#ev-2025-peaceful-alternation-of-power, claim TL:MWI:event:2025:peaceful-alternation-of-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
